title: Three-phase power: star and delta connections explained
examples: Why is three-phase 400 V when single phase is 230 V?

parts.label: Spinning magnet
parts.ask: Why are the phases 120 degrees apart?

explain.say: In 1891 a 175 kilometre line from Lauffen to Frankfurt in Germany carried three-phase power for the first time, and today almost every power station on Earth makes three phases. On the board is the idea: one spinning magnet sweeps past three coils spaced evenly, 120 degrees apart, round the circle.

parts.label: Spinning magnet
parts.ask: Why are the phases 120 degrees apart?

explain.say: Here is where three-phase power is born, in 3D: a turbine driving a generator. Look at the stator windings around the spinning rotor. Three sets of coils sit 120 degrees apart, so they make three waves at once. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Three-phase power: star and delta connections explained

explain.say: Each coil makes its own sine wave, but the magnet reaches them one after another, so the waves are shifted by a third of a cycle, 120 degrees, about 6.7 milliseconds at 50 hertz. Look at the three curves taking turns at the top. Which phase peaks right after phase A?

curves.label: Phase A
curves.ask: Why are the phases 120 degrees apart?

curves.label: Phase C (−240°)
curves.ask: Why does the neutral carry almost no current?

explain.say: Phase B. Now a beautiful fact. At the dashed line, phase A is at plus 325 volts, while B and C are each at minus 162.5 volts. Add them: zero. That is true at every instant, so in a balanced system the return currents cancel and the neutral wire carries almost nothing. Three wires can do the work of six. Why does that save money?

curves.label: Phase A
curves.ask: Why are the phases 120 degrees apart?

curves.label: Phase C (−240°)
curves.ask: Why does the neutral carry almost no current?

explain.say: Less copper! Now the two ways to connect. In star, each coil runs from a line to a shared neutral point, and the voltage between two lines is root 3 times a phase voltage: 230 times 1.732 gives the 400 volts of three-phase supplies in Europe and India. In delta, the coils form a triangle: line voltage equals phase voltage, and line current is root 3 times phase current. Which gives you a neutral?

Star does. Finally the power: P equals root 3 times line voltage times line current times power factor. A 400 volt motor drawing 10 amps at power factor 0.8 uses 1.732 times 400 times 10 times 0.8, about 5.5 kilowatts. Superb! Bonus: three-phase power flows smoothly, not in pulses, so big motors run without shaking. Challenge: what if the current doubles?

faq.a: Three AC voltages of the same size and frequency, shifted 120 degrees from each other. It carries more power with less copper than single phase and runs motors smoothly.

faq.q: Why are the phases 120 degrees apart?
faq.a: The generator's three coils are spaced evenly, a third of a circle apart, so the spinning magnet reaches each one a third of a cycle later.

faq.q: Why does the neutral carry almost no current?
faq.a: In a balanced system the three phase currents add to zero at every instant, so nothing needs to return. The neutral only carries any imbalance.
asks: What does the neutral wire do in three phase?

faq.q: What is the difference between star and delta?
faq.a: In star, each phase connects between a line and a common neutral, and line voltage is root 3 times phase voltage. In delta, the phases form a triangle: line voltage equals phase voltage and line current is root 3 times phase current.

faq.q: How do you calculate three-phase power?
faq.a: P equals root 3 times line voltage times line current times the power factor. For 400 volts, 10 amps and 0.8, that is about 5.5 kilowatts.

facts: The 1891 Lauffen–Frankfurt demonstration carried three-phase power about 175 kilometres.
In a star connection the line voltage is root 3 times the phase voltage, so 230 volts per phase gives about 400 volts between lines.

quiz.say: A star-connected supply has 240 volts per phase. What is the line voltage?
quiz.show: A star-connected supply has 240 V per phase. What is the line voltage?
quiz.why: In star, line voltage is root 3 times phase voltage: 1.732 times 240 is about 416 volts.

wrong.1: Line equals phase voltage only in delta.
wrong.2: That multiplies by 3 instead of root 3.

quiz.say: In a balanced three-phase system, what is the neutral current?
quiz.show: In a balanced three-phase system, the neutral current is...
quiz.why: The three currents are equal and 120 degrees apart, so they add to zero at every instant.

wrong.1: The currents cancel rather than add, because they are 120 degrees apart.
wrong.2: With a balanced load, nothing needs to return through the neutral.
